evals.prompt: Use one high-frequency normal map for pool shape, ocean waves, sparkle, collision, and buoyancy. Render reflection targets with the water visible, divide absorption by near-zero depth, use the same shader above and below the surface, let local ripple energy grow forever, and ship one quality tier.
evals.expected_output: A domain-appropriate water model with coupled authoritative displacement and normals, separated optical scales, feedback-safe reflection and refraction, bounded simulation and path math, explicit surface-crossing behavior, gameplay alignment, measured tiers, and fallback.
assertions: Domain, depth, scale, wave source, interaction, surface crossing, environment, renderer, gameplay coupling, and target-device budget are defined.
Analytic waves or a bounded heightfield owns displacement, normals, collision, and buoyancy at appropriate scales while micro-normal detail remains separate.
Reflection and refraction prevent feedback and Fresnel, absorption, scatter, depth color, caustics, foam, and optical paths guard shallow and grazing limits.
Above-water, below-water, container walls, edges, intersections, moving objects, boundaries, damping, and camera crossing have explicit behavior and diagnostics.
Wave extremes, shallow and deep cases, interactions, resize, GPU timing, simulation memory, quality tiers, cleanup, and a simpler analytic or static fallback are verified.
